anomaly_def.Name: Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly: The engine allocates more RAM or swap for buffer caches, work areas, plan cache, background heaps, and other regions than the host can safely supply, triggering paging, OOM events, and cache churn.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly: The physical read/write demand on the underlying storage subsystem reaches or exceeds its sustained bandwidth, IOPS, or latency limits, producing long device queues and high wait times.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly: The free physical or logical capacity of data, temp, log, or backup volumes falls to critical levels, provoking allocation failures, halted extensions, or log-archive stalls.

When all three anomalies co-exist, the database is under-provisioned in every core resource dimension—memory, bandwidth, and capacity—causing a reinforcing spiral of resource contention. Symptoms include: relentless growth of the database process RSS followed by operating-system paging that floods the storage layer; soaring read/write latency with queues pegged as memory shortfalls force more buffer evictions, re-reads, and large temp spills; sudden or intermittent "out of space" errors as emergency temp and redo growth consume the last free blocks; erratic query performance, prolonged checkpoints, stalled commits, and unplanned node reboots that complicate diagnosis because wait events for memory, I/O, and space failure interleave in monitoring snapshots.

Causally, excessive memory allocation fills RAM, causing the OS to swap, which multiplies I/O traffic and immediately stresses storage throughput. The overwhelmed storage layer slows page-in operations, lengthening memory stalls and encouraging the engine to evict clean buffers more aggressively, which in turn amplifies read churn. Simultaneously, temp spills from under-sized work memory and prolonged log flushes inflate data and log files, accelerating consumption of already scarce disk space. As space dwindles, auto-extension or archive operations may hang, holding locks and freezing writers, which further prolongs transactions and retains even more memory. The mutual amplification among memory pressure, I/O saturation, and space exhaustion can culminate in system-wide deadlocks, forced shutdowns, or data-loss situations if not promptly mitigated.

entry.official_definition: Maximum wait for connection, in seconds; zero or not specified means wait indefinitely.
entry.trigger_condition: A libpq client connection attempt exceeds connect_timeout seconds.
entry.workload_impact: The client connection attempt fails instead of waiting indefinitely.
entry.default_behavior: Zero or absent value means wait indefinitely.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
